example:
A model finishes with prose but no `submit_result` call: the harness reminds
it once, and when it then calls `submit_result`, the agent request succeeds. When
it ends with prose again, the request fails. The same reminder applies to a
response with multiple `submit_result` calls. A single call with invalid
arguments receives a tool error so the model can correct the submission.
{test}`requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission.reminder`
rationale: Add `{test}` to `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tests.rs#fn[malformed_submissions_receive_feedback_and_can_be_corrected]` — The example's last outcome says a single `submit_result` call with invalid arguments receives a tool error so the model can correct it. The referenced tests do not assert that. The example's other outcomes are covered: a reminder then success (`the_agent_can_submit_after_the_missing_submission_reminder`, `count_is_checked_before_arguments_and_one_reminder_allows_recovery`), prose again failing (`missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence` with empty calls, which checks 'even after a reminder'), and multiple calls getting the same reminder (`count_is_checked_before_arguments_and_one_reminder_allows_recovery`). The only referenced test with a single invalid call is `missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence`. It only checks that a second request is made. It never reads that request for a tool-error result, and the second turn is a provider 400, so no correction is accepted. A harness that reminded the model, or sent any other follow-up, would pass it. `malformed_submissions_receive_feedback_and_can_be_corrected` fills this gap. It sends a single invalid `submit_result` call and asserts that the next request carries an error tool result with a diagnostic and 'Resubmit'. It then accepts the corrected submission. It currently cites only `agent-harness.submission.invalid`, so it should also be a `{test}` reference for `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-harness.submission_count`.
